authoredSolutions.62: \(3a-3a+\sqrt7=\sqrt7\) is irrational, so reflexive. With \(a-b=\sqrt7/3:\ (a,b)\in R\) but \(3(b-a)+\sqrt7=0\) is rational so \((b,a)\notin R\): not symmetric. A chain \((a,b),(b,c)\in R\) can give \(3(a-c)+\sqrt7\) rational: not transitive. Hence reflexive only.

authoredSolutions.180: With the \(\tfrac{5^{\cos x}}{1+5^{\cos x}}\) king-property over \([0,\pi]\) (\(x\to\pi-x\) leaves \(N=1+\cos x\cos3x+\cos^2x+\cos^3x\cos3x\) invariant), \(I=\tfrac12\int_0^\pi N\,dx\). \(\int_0^\pi N=\pi+0+\tfrac\pi2+\tfrac\pi8=\tfrac{13\pi}{8}\), so \(I=\tfrac{13\pi}{16}\Rightarrow k=13\).
